A1.justification: Both 35-page PDFs describe the same RF-Deep research. The main text, 12 tables, 15 figures, equations, and Appendices A–D are readable and can be matched despite layout changes.

before.justification: v3 reports original segmentation and OOD-detection experiments on 2,232 CT volumes, including blinded validation, ablations, robustness tests, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices, including benchmark comparisons, blinded validation, and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The frozen segmentation backbone, tumor-anchored feature extraction, random forest with outlier exposure, and deployment strategies remain unchanged. Rewording the architecture and handling of absent predictions does not alter the procedure.

E1.justification: Section 4.2 retains the same pretraining, fine-tuning, lung-cancer ID, four primary OOD, and two blinded-validation datasets. Describing chest scans as 'thoracic (chest)' adds no coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across corresponding experiments: MaxSoftmax, MaxLogit, Energy, RF-Radiomics, MD-Deep, classifier alternatives, and the ReAct, ASH, and X-Mahalanobis comparisons in Appendix C.

E3.justification: The versions retain the same splits, sample counts, preprocessing, backbone configurations, training budgets, and DSC, HD95, AUROC, and FPR95 evaluation procedures. No additional experimental protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: Both retain the foreground-volume and absent-prediction analyses, SHAP and clustering analyses, deployment and acquisition robustness tests, and ROI, crop, exposure-size, encoder-stage, and comparator ablations. Relocated displays contain existing analyses.

E5.justification: Both already report 100 matched-seed runs, 95% bootstrap confidence intervals, and the same correlation and significance tests. The new sentence in Figure 4's caption repeats existing uncertainty information rather than introducing a reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Section 5.2.2 changes the reported Swin UNETR near-OOD AUROC gap from '4–7%' to '4–7 percentage points,' clarifying the quantitative comparison's units. Corresponding Table 12 scores and all other matched numerical and plotted results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B retains the same softmax, predicted-foreground set, and MaxSoftmax, MaxLogit, and Energy score definitions. Equations are compressed into inline presentation without changing their mathematics; no assumptions or proofs are revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about limited-exposure post-hoc detection, near- and far-OOD performance, backbone robustness, and blinded transferability.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 recasts some discrimination and robustness assertions as design intentions. The Broader Impact Statement narrows the anticipated benefit from reducing patient harm to reducing inappropriate downstream decisions. Existing mechanisms and limitations remain.

D1.justification: Implementation, hyperparameter, preprocessing, pretraining, hardware, and runtime disclosures remain unchanged, including Appendix A and Table 10. The added OpenReview link supplies publication metadata, not new code or data access.

R1.justification: The reference lists are identical, and the related-work discussion retains the same research positioning. Expanding PCA and adding publication metadata introduce no new cited work or novelty claim.

P1.justification: Localized copyediting clarifies terminology, architecture prose, deployment descriptions, and percentage-point wording. v4 also adds publication/review information and acknowledged contributors, while retaining the section and appendix organization.

P2.justification: v4 adds publication headers, relocates Table 6, Figure 11, and Tables 8–9, and makes Appendix B's score equations inline. Figure 4 gains a confidence-interval sentence despite displaying CT slices. The underlying figure content and table values are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 offers small clarity gains through explicit percentage-point wording and more cautious deployment and clinical-impact language. Scientific support remains unchanged, while the new confidence-interval sentence is misplaced in Figure 4's CT-image caption. These limited refinements and the caption defect leave overall quality essentially unchanged.
